- **Zero Trust guidelines**: NSA released Phase One and Phase Two of Zero Trust Implementation Guidelines to help organizations improve cybersecurity standards.[1][7]
- **International collaboration**: NSA partnered with the Australian Signals Directorate and other agencies on satellite communications security (March 24, 2026).[1]
- **Cyber policy debate**: Four NSA directors convened (March 24, 2026) to discuss American offensive cyber warfare capabilities and autonomous AI agents.[2]
- **Surveillance concerns**: Ongoing discussions about Section 702 reauthorization (expiring April 2026) focus on warrantless surveillance of communications and FBI's use of the law for domestic law enforcement without warrants.[4][5]
- **Compliance violations**: Declassified reports document past NSA surveillance rule violations but involve communications interception, not mind control.[6]

Mind control narratives are conspiracy theories without substantiation in official intelligence community reports or credible journalism.
